clue.text: Obtain power, energy inside

indicators.note: the energy letter is placed within the word for power, so inside marks the container

parts.note: to drive is to power something along
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A physics instruction: get power by putting energy into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive something is to get or extract it from a source, so it is a synonym of obtain.

clue.text: Resolve to get rid of one in the most terrible form of murder?

indicators.note: the clue tells you to remove one letter from the murder word, so this phrase signals a deletion

parts.words: the most terrible form of murder
parts.note: deicide, the killing of a god, is jokingly the worst murder imaginable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone resolving to avoid committing the worst sort of killing.
explanation.walkthrough: DEICIDE is the killing of a god; the question mark admits the 'most terrible' description is the setter's opinion. Taking out one I leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve on something is to make up your mind about it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Return when nothing's left — worker on the scrap heap?

indicators.note: read as 'left out', the word nothing being dropped from the return word signals a deletion

parts.note: to redound is to come back or recoil on someone
nothing is the letter O, a zero; the 's is 'is'
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: A laid-off labourer coming back to find nothing remains for them.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'nothing's left' as 'nothing is left out', so the zero letter is dropped; 'when' only joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the scrap heap has been laid off as no longer needed, which is what being made surplus means.

clue.text: Vigour needed to contain potentially explosive situation in country

indicators.note: the vigour word has to hold the volcano within it, so this marks a container

parts.note: vim means vigour or energy
Etna is the active volcano in Sicily, a literally explosive place

explanation.surface: Energetic diplomacy is needed to keep a volatile crisis under control in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'potentially explosive situation' looks like a political crisis, but it is a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a nation in South-East Asia, an example of a country.

clue.text: Vandal having instrument destroyed, almost

parts.note: the viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: almost means the destroyed word stops one letter short of the end

parts.note: torn means ripped apart or destroyed

explanation.surface: A hooligan who has smashed a musical instrument nearly beyond repair.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal breaks or desecrates things, and someone who violates property or a sacred place does the same.

clue.text: Mix when at university, say, in front of a fire

indicators.note: the first piece goes in front of the second in a down entry, so this orders the charade

parts.note: students are 'in term' while at university, and 'say' marks this as one example of being in term
an ingle is a fire on a domestic hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Students mingling in front of a fire while at college.
explanation.walkthrough: An ingle is an old Scots word for a hearth fire, preserved in 'inglenook'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermingle is to blend or mix together, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Temper evident when sea captain loses head in front of a number

indicators.note: the shortened name comes before the number, which fixes the order of the charade
the captain's name drops its first letter, so losing a head signals removing the opening letter

parts.note: Captain William Bligh commanded HMS Bounty at the time of the famous mutiny
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A sea captain's bad mood is obvious as he loses his head in front of his crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like anger, but it is the verb meaning moderate; 'evident when' joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper a thing is to moderate it or make it less severe, which is a sense of easing or making lighter.

clue.text: A lecturer joining group — revolutionary physics unit

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the joined pieces are read backwards up the down entry

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A lecturer joins a group of radical scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: A, L and SET together are written backwards because of 'revolutionary', a nod to the inventor of the alternating-current motor.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is named after the inventor Nikola, so it is a unit used in physics.

clue.text: Sold with a new bit added on at the end?

definitions.meaning: goods ... have been sold to the public in a shop

definitions.text: with a new bit added on at the end?
definitions.meaning: given a tail again, a new piece at the rear

explanation.surface: An item sold after someone attached a fresh extension to its end.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as RE-TAILED, given another tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailing is selling goods to the public, so the past form fits sold.

clue.text: Geezer around back of building is computer programmer

indicators.note: the programmer word goes around the letter from the building, so around marks a container

parts.note: a coder writes computer code

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here the last letter of building

explanation.surface: An old man hanging around the rear of an office block turns out to write software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Geezer' is British slang for a man, and here an old one.
explanation.definitionFit: A codger is an elderly man, and geezer is informal for an old fellow, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Get seats organised — a must for the play

indicators.note: seats that are organised are rearranged, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre manager tells staff to arrange the audience chairs before the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenery built on the boards is something a theatre production needs, so it is described as essential.

clue.text: Information on fare for journey will be given here

definitions.text: Information on fare for journey will be given here

parts.words: Information on fare for journey will be given here
parts.note: fare looks like the ticket price, but it means food; the menu for a train trip is found in the carriage where meals are served

explanation.surface: A notice at a station saying where to ask about ticket prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests the cost of travel, but here it means food served on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage where passengers eat is where the meal choices for the trip are shown.

clue.text: Holiday location that could do for coolest lads

indicators.note: something that could do for the given letters is a rearranged form standing in for them

explanation.surface: A beach resort that would suit the trendiest young men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could do for' reads as 'would suit' but means the letters can be reshaped into the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish coast around Málaga is a popular package-holiday destination.

clue.text: Meal from a Far Eastern country left to be eaten

indicators.note: the left letter is eaten by the country word, swallowed inside it, so this marks a container

parts.note: Thai means from Thailand

explanation.surface: A dish from an Asian nation with leftovers waiting to be finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A thali is an Indian meal served as a selection of small dishes on a platter.

clue.text: A welcome sign for anyone who hasn't got ready?

definitions.text: A welcome sign for anyone who hasn't got ready?

parts.words: A welcome sign for anyone who hasn't got ready?
parts.note: ready is slang for cash, so someone without money is glad to see a notice saying entry costs nothing

explanation.surface: A cheerful notice for someone who is not yet prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like 'prepared' but is British slang for money (the 'readies').
explanation.definitionFit: A notice saying entry costs nothing is welcome to someone with no cash.

clue.text: Fruit — mash or else pap

indicators.note: to mash is to crush and mix up, so the letters are thoroughly rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook offering a choice: fruit, or else mash it into baby food.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose apple is a tropical fruit with a rose-scented flavour, an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Examination not fair when one's restricted by wind!

indicators.note: the one letter is held in by the wind word around it, so this marks a container

parts.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind in southern France
I is the Roman numeral for one; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A complaint that a test was unfair because a gale held the candidate back.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial ruled invalid through an error is an unfair legal examination of a case.

clue.text: Old-style entertainment has magnetism, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or altered, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone thinks an old-fashioned show has real charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' reads as 'I think', but 'fancy' alone is the anagram signal, with I in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: These were athletic festivals held at Corinth in ancient Greece, so very old-style entertainment.

clue.text: Drama in which Bill and little woman get married at the start

indicators.note: the married letter is placed before the other pieces, at the start of the entry

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
Beth is one of the March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A play in which a man and a young woman wed in the opening scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' points to Beth March of Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Shakespeare's Scottish tragedy, an example of a drama.

clue.text: Pick dull-looking wine, not the top one

parts.note: matt describes a surface without shine

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so the wine word loses its opening letter

parts.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A choice of a drab bottle of wine, though not the best one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' looks like choose, but it is the noun for a digging tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattock is a digging tool like a pickaxe with a broad blade, so it is a kind of pick.

clue.text: Teacher embarrassed — knocked over plant

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the pieces are read in reverse up the down entry

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: A red-faced teacher who toppled a potted plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Derris is a tropical climbing plant whose roots yield an insecticide.

clue.text: We may discuss this item of headgear, having got cold

parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet, a pith hat
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: People talk about a hat that has caught a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject of discussion is what people talk about, so it is the thing we may discuss.

clue.text: Instruction from composer shown briefly at start of prelude

definitions.text: Instruction from composer shown briefly at start of prelude

parts.words: Instruction from composer shown briefly at start of prelude
parts.note: the marking telling players to play softly is abbreviated to p, the letter at the start of prelude

explanation.surface: A direction from the composer is written in short form at the opening of a prelude.
explanation.walkthrough: Shown briefly, the direction is the single letter p, which is literally the start of 'prelude'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical direction tells performers to play quietly.

clue.text: Happen to be in flat by gallery outside university

parts.note: even means flat or level

indicators.note: the gallery word sits outside the university letter, holding it, so this marks a container

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone happens to live in a flat next to an art gallery beyond the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' reads as an apartment but means level; 'to be in' and 'by' join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To eventuate is to result or come to pass, a formal synonym of occur.

clue.text: Looking from a particular angle, see inn as wicked

indicators.note: wicked letters behave badly and are jumbled, so this signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: From one point of view, a pub may be seen as a den of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'in one way of looking at it', viewing something from a certain perspective.

clue.text: Funny Tommy who rolled out the barrel?

definitions.meaning: Tommy ... was a British comedian famous for his bungled magic tricks and fez
a barrel-maker would roll out each finished barrel from the workshop

explanation.surface: A comic who sang 'Roll Out the Barrel'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll Out the Barrel' is a song, but here the barrel is literal, made by a cask-maker; Tommy Cooper was a much-loved British TV comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the comic Tommy is also the trade name for a maker of barrels and casks.

clue.text: Deficiency in lavatory rod restricting flush finally

parts.note: loo is British informal for a lavatory

indicators.note: the rod word restricts, or hems in, the last letter of flush, so this marks a container

parts.note: a pole is a rod

indicators.note: finally takes only the final letter of the word flush

explanation.surface: A fault in a toilet's lever is getting in the way of the flush.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a gap or flaw in a rule that lets someone evade it, a kind of deficiency.

clue.text: They go up and they come down

definitions.text: They go up and they come down

parts.words: They go up and they come down
parts.note: people on the slopes ride the lift up and then descend on snow, a description that sounds like a riddle

explanation.surface: A riddle about things that rise and fall.
explanation.definitionFit: People on a ski holiday take lifts up the mountain and then slide back down.
